paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the seed is the same every time. The farmer doesn't toss out four different kinds of seed. What changes is the soil, and Jesus says the soil is the heart of the one who hears (Matthew 13:19-23). So the question for you and me is not whether the word is good. It's what is going on in the ground where it lands.

Look at the ways the word gets lost. On the path, the evil one "snatches away what was sown" (Matthew 13:19). On the rocky ground, the one who receives it with joy has "no root," so when trouble comes he "quickly falls away" (Matthew 13:20-21). Among the thorns, "the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word" (Matthew 13:22). Friend, I know that thorn patch. A bad week and a full calendar can crowd out a lot of good seed, so I think Jesus is saying: deep roots and a clear patch matter MORE than a big first smile.

Now the good news, and it's LOUD: the good soil is the one who "hears the word and understands it," and he "bears fruit" (Matthew 13:23). Jesus also tells His disciples, "blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear" (Matthew 13:16). So here's what I'm baking into you, friend: come to the word to hear it AND understand it, and let it go deep. Jesus says, "He who has ears, let him hear" (Matthew 13:9), and I plan to keep my ears wide open. The story isn't over, because Jesus has more to say about the kingdom.
